context:
Build on the Phase 1 foundation. The static build pipeline already transforms
bundles into read models - Phase 2 just adds more bundles from community PRs.
The `benchbox submit` command is a thin packaging layer, not a new code path.
description:
Phase 2 of the results platform: enable community contributions via a
PR-based submission model. Instead of building a hosted API, contributors
use `benchbox submit --output ./submission/` to package a result bundle
with a submission manifest, then open a PR against this repository touching
`results-data/`.

GitHub Actions CI validates the submission (schema, hash, cohort, sanity).
Maintainers review and merge. Merge triggers a rebuild of derived read
models and redeployment of the explorer.

This model uses GitHub as the auth, moderation, and audit layer - zero
hosted services required. It scales to ~100s of submissions/month before
maintainer review becomes a bottleneck.

**Contingency:** This TODO should only be started after Phase 1 has launched
and the explorer UX is validated with real users. If Phase 1 reveals that
the data model or explorer architecture needs significant changes, those
changes should be made before opening community contributions.

anti_patterns.dont: auto-merge community submissions without maintainer review
build a hosted API for Phase 2
anti_patterns.why: PR-based submission is sufficient until volume demands it

preserves.behavior: Existing benchbox run/export workflows are not modified
Phase 1 explorer continues to work for maintainer-curated results
The canonical schema-v2 bundle remains the submission artifact - no alternative format

verifications.description: benchbox submit --output packages a valid submission bundle
CI validation workflow catches invalid submissions

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run build && grep -l 'Community Submitted' dist/r/*/index.html | head -1
verifications.description: Trust labels render correctly in the explorer
verifications.expected: At least one detail page with community label

work_units.notes:
Define the submission package format:
- Canonical schema-v2 bundle (required)
- Companion files: .plans.json, .tuning.json (optional)
- submission-manifest.json:
  - contributor: name/handle (from git config or explicit)
  - context: why this result is interesting (optional free text)
  - platform_notes: hardware/cloud context not captured in bundle
  - submission_date: ISO timestamp
The package is a directory that can be directly committed to the data repo.
work_units.summary: Design submission manifest schema and packaging format

work_units.notes:
Add a CLI command that packages an existing exported result bundle into
the submission format:
1. Takes a result bundle path (or --last to use most recent)
2. Prompts for optional contributor info and context
3. Writes submission package to the specified output directory
4. Prints instructions for opening a PR against the current results corpus location

This command does NOT upload anything. It only packages locally.

Create a GitHub Actions workflow in this repo that runs on PRs touching
`results-data/`:
- Schema validation: bundle conforms to schema-v2
- Hash verification: bundle content matches declared hash
- Cohort compatibility: benchmark/scale/query-set are valid
- Sanity checks: no absurd timings (e.g., 0ms for all queries),
  valid platform names, reasonable environment metadata
- Diff summary: comment on PR with what would be added to the explorer
work_units.summary: Build CI validation workflow for submission PRs

work_units.notes:
Update the static build pipeline and explorer to show trust labels:
- "Maintainer Run" badge for results generated by BenchBox CI
- "Community Submitted" badge for results from merged PRs
The source is determined by commit author or a field in the submission manifest.
Badges appear on detail pages, browse pages, and compare views.
work_units.summary: Add trust labels to the explorer for community-submitted results
